questions.question: A person can walk at a speed of 0.5 meters/second. How far will he walk in 8 minutes?

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest (compounding annually) and simple interest on a sum at the rate of 30 percent per annum for 2 years is Rs. 3600. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given directly by the formula:

Difference = P × (R / 100)²

3600 = P × (30 / 100)²

3600 = P × (9 / 100) ⇒ P = 40000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 40000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 30% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Difference between CI and SI = Rs. 3600

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2b5620dd21648c6c1e52f210c7ca4bd851c2ceb5f8ed3540bf41c2bb9e7fdff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective Simple Interest rate for 2 years = 30% × 2 = 60%

⇒ Effective Compound Interest rate for 2 years = X + Y + (X × Y) / 100

⇒ Effective CI rate = 30% + 30% + (30 × 30) / 100 % = 69%

⇒ Difference in percentage = 69% − 60% = 9%

⇒ According to the question, 9% of the Principal corresponds to Rs. 3600

⇒ 1% of Principal = 3600 ÷ 9 = 400

⇒ Total Sum (100% Principal) = 400 × 100 = 40000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 40000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective CI rate can be found using successive percentage formula: [2R + (R² ÷ 100)]%. The term (R² ÷ 100)% directly gives the difference between CI and SI in percentage.

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is calculated using the standard formula: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods, which creates the difference over time.

questions.question: X, Y and Z enter into a partnership. X invests some money at the beginning. Y Invests thrice the amount of X after 4 months and Z invest double the amount of Y after 9 months from the beginning. If the annual gain be Rs. 450000, then what is the share of Y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = (Capital × Time)

X : Y : Z = (1 × 12) : (3 × 8) : (6 × 3) = 12 : 24 : 18 = 2 : 4 : 3

Total profit ratio = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 parts

9 parts = Rs. 450000 ⇒ 1 part = Rs. 50000

Share of Y = 4 parts = 4 × 50000 = Rs. 200000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total annual gain = Rs. 450000

Y joins after 4 months and Z joins after 9 months from the beginning.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Investment × Time

 
 Partner X
 Capital = P | Time = 12m
 Profit = 12P

 
 Partner Y
 Capital = 3P | Time = 8m
 Profit = 24P

 
 Partner Z
 Capital = 6P | Time = 3m
 Profit = 18P

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial investment of X = P

⇒ Investment of Y = 3P

⇒ Investment of Z = 2 × 3P = 6P

⇒ Time for X = 12 months

⇒ Time for Y = 12 − 4 = 8 months

⇒ Time for Z = 12 − 9 = 3 months

⇒ Profit of X = P × 12 = 12P

⇒ Profit of Y = 3P × 8 = 24P

⇒ Profit of Z = 6P × 3 = 18P

⇒ Ratio of Profit (X : Y : Z) = 12P : 24P : 18P = 2 : 4 : 3

⇒ Total ratio parts = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 parts

⇒ 9 parts = Rs. 450000

⇒ 1 part = 450000 ÷ 9 = Rs. 50000

⇒ Share of Y = 4 parts = 4 × 50000 = Rs. 200000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit in Partnership

When partners invest varying capitals for different periods, the profit is divided in the ratio of the product of capital and time. Formula: Profit Ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and receives a salary or fixed percentage of profit as remuneration, whereas a sleeping partner only invests capital and shares the remaining profit strictly according to their investment ratio.

Compound Partnership

If partners alter their investments during the business term by adding or withdrawing capital, the profit distribution is based on the sum of the products of their capital amounts and the respective time periods for which each capital remained invested.
</p

questions.question: The main minerals constituents of the continental mass are ________ and ________.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'silica, alumina'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silica (SiO₂) and Alumina (Al₂O₃):**

 
 
• The continental crust is primarily composed of silicate minerals, which are rich in silica and alumina.
 
• These compounds form the bulk of minerals such as feldspar and quartz, which are the most abundant minerals in the Earth's continental crust.
 
• Silica (SiO₂) contributes to the crust’s overall light color and low density, characteristic of continental rocks.
 
• Alumina (Al₂O₃) is a key component of feldspar minerals, which make up about 60% of the Earth's crust.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxygen and Carbon:**

 
 
• Oxygen is indeed a major component of continental crust minerals, making up about 46.6% of the crust by weight.
 
• Carbon, however, is present in much smaller quantities mainly in carbonate minerals, which are much less abundant in the continental crust compared to silicate minerals.
 
 
 
• **Silica and Magnesium:**
 
 
• While silica is a major component of the continental crust, magnesium is more prevalent in the Earth's mantle and oceanic crust.
 
• Minerals such as olivine and pyroxene, which are rich in magnesium, are found primarily in the mantle and oceanic crust rather than in the continental crust.
 
 
 
• **Alumina and Magnesium:**
 
 
• Alumina is a significant component of the continental crust, but pairing it with magnesium overlooks the dominant presence of silica in the continental crust rocks.
 
• Magnesium, similar to the previous point, is more associated with deeper parts of the Earth's structure such as the mantle and oceanic crust.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The composition of the continental crust is crucial for understanding various geological and geochemical processes.
 
• The predominance of silica and alumina gives the continental crust its unique characteristics, such as lower density and different mineralogy compared to the oceanic crust.
 
• This knowledge is fundamental in the study of plate tectonics, mountain-building processes, and the formation of different rock types.

questions.question: Which component of the cell organelles principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golgi Apparatus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Golgi Apparatus:

 
 
• The Golgi apparatus has multiple names such as the Golgi complex or Golgi body.
 
• The name is given on the name of the scientist, who discovered the organelle, i.e. Camillo Golgi.
 
• It is found in all eukaryotic cells, plants as well as animals.
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles present in the cytosol of the cell.
 
• The Golgi body comprises 5 to 8-cup-shaped, series of compartments known as cisternae. Cisternae is a flattened, disk-shaped, stacked pouches that make up the Golgi apparatus. A Golgi stack mostly contains 4 to 8 cisternae. However, ~60 cisternae are found in some protists. A mammalian cell contains ~40 to 100 stacks of cisternae.
 
• Animal cells generally contain around 10 to 20 Golgi stacks per cell, which are connected by tubular connections.
 
• The Golgi complex is mostly found near the nucleus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9501690c5324825b9c437459e780de7351fe3f51e4982825d01d58711e338499.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**.

 
 
• The number of mitochondria in a single cell may be up to 50 to 5000.
 
• The inner lumen of mitochondria contains ribosome phosphate particles and DNA molecules.
 
• It has the potential to synthesize its own protein and oxidation of carbohydrates and fats are taken place with the help of enzymes in mitochondria.
 
• This energy is stored in the form of ATP ( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the "Powerhouse of the cell".​
 
 
 
• Chloroplast:

• Out of the two membranes, the inner membrane is relatively less permeable. (the outer membrane contains porins).
